facts.fact: State legislative ad spending is projected to reach $700 million in 2026, a 19% jump from 2024, according to Axios (September 2025), as cited by AdWave.
facts.quote: In 2026, state legislative ad spending is projected to reach $700 million, a 19% jump from 2024

facts.fact: Seven states are expected to see more than $50 million invested in state-level races alone.
facts.quote: Seven states are expected to see more than $50 million invested in state-level races alone.

facts.fact: Streaming accounts for over 44% of all TV viewing, per Arena Wins Blog (March 2025) as cited by AdWave.
facts.quote: Streaming now accounts for over 44% of all TV viewing

facts.fact: 84% of swing voters are reachable through streaming TV compared to 63% on linear TV, per Arena Wins Blog (March 2025).
facts.quote: 84% of swing voters are reachable through streaming TV compared to just 63% on linear

facts.fact: The 2026 midterm cycle is projected to reach $10.8 billion in total political ad spending, per OpenSecrets (January 2026).
facts.quote: The 2026 midterm cycle is projected to hit $10.8 billion in total political ad spending

facts.fact: Through January 2026, $2.01 billion in political ad spending had been spent, a 46% increase over the same point in the 2022 cycle.
facts.quote: Through January 2026, $2.01 billion had already been spent, a 46% increase over the same point in the 2022 cycle.

facts.fact: Political advertisers are expected to spend $2.48 billion on streaming TV in 2026, up from $1.09 billion in the 2022 midterms, per The Current (2026).
facts.quote: Political advertisers are expected to spend $2.48 billion on streaming TV in 2026, up from $1.09 billion in the 2022 midterms

facts.fact: Political streaming TV spending is described as a 127% increase in four years.
facts.quote: That's a 127% increase in just four years.

facts.fact: Downballot contests and state legislative races account for $3.9 billion in projected 2026 spending, more than a third of the total, per OpenSecrets (January 2026); this figure includes digital and print.
facts.quote: Downballot contests and state legislative races account for $3.9 billion in projected spending for 2026, more than a third of the total

facts.fact: AdWave's budget tier for small rural or suburban state legislature districts is a total budget of $50,000-$150,000 with 30-40% allocated to TV.
AdWave's budget tier for mid-size state legislature districts is a total budget of $150,000-$500,000 with 40-50% allocated to TV.
AdWave's budget tier for competitive or urban state legislature districts is a total budget of $500,000-$2M+ with 50-60% allocated to TV.
Some streaming platforms allow campaigns to launch for as little as $50, per AdWave.
facts.quote: with some allowing campaigns to launch for as little as $50.

facts.fact: AdWave describes the name-recognition phase of a state legislature TV campaign as running 3-4 months before the election.
facts.quote: Phase 1: Name recognition (3-4 months before election)

facts.fact: AdWave describes the issue-positioning phase as running 6-8 weeks before the election.
facts.quote: Phase 2: Issue positioning (6-8 weeks before election)

facts.fact: AdWave describes the persuasion and GOTV phase as the final 2-3 weeks before the election.
facts.quote: Phase 3: Persuasion and GOTV (final 2-3 weeks)

facts.fact: Broadcast TV buys a full designated market area (DMA), so a district covering 15% of a DMA's population means roughly 85% of spend reaches non-constituents, per AdWave's illustration.
facts.quote: If your district covers 15% of a DMA's population, roughly 85% of your ad dollars reach people who can't even vote for you.

facts.fact: The Adwave guide recommends a 60/40 budget split favoring CTV over broadcast as a starting point for most competitive state legislature races in 2026.
facts.quote: a 60/40 split favoring CTV over broadcast is a good starting point

facts.fact: The Adwave guide recommends allocating 70-80% to CTV and 20-30% to broadcast when the district skews younger (under 45).
facts.quote: Skews younger (under 45) | 70-80% | 20-30%

facts.fact: The Adwave guide recommends allocating 40-50% to CTV and 50-60% to broadcast when the district skews older (55+).
According to Arena Wins (March 2025), 28% of swing voters are exclusively reachable via streaming, while 18% are exclusively on linear TV.
facts.quote: 28% of swing voters are exclusively reachable via streaming, while 18% are exclusively on linear TV

facts.fact: According to Innovid (2025), CTV ads typically see 90-98% completion rates, far higher than digital video.
facts.quote: CTV ads typically see 90-98% completion rates, far higher than digital video

facts.fact: Adwave states that campaigns can create and launch TV ads through its platform starting at $50.
facts.quote: let campaigns create and launch TV ads starting at just $50

facts.fact: The Adwave guide suggests that even $500-$1,000 per month can build meaningful reach in a targeted district.
facts.quote: Even $500-$1,000 per month can build meaningful reach in a targeted district

facts.fact: The Adwave guide states that broadcast TV in a major metro can cost $5,000 or more per week.
facts.quote: Broadcast TV in a major metro can cost $5,000 or more per week

facts.fact: The Adwave guide recommends starting political CTV advertising six months before Election Day for competitive races.
facts.quote: For competitive races, starting six months before Election Day gives you time to build name recognition

facts.fact: According to the Adwave guide, for federal races a "stand by your ad" statement is typically required when the candidate appears in the ad, though state rules vary.
facts.quote: If the candidate appears in the ad, a "stand by your ad" statement is typically required for federal races (state rules vary)

facts.fact: The Adwave guide states that stations must maintain public files of political ad purchases as a federal record-keeping requirement.
facts.quote: Record keeping:** Stations must maintain public files of political ad purchases

facts.fact: At minimum, all political ads need a "paid for by" disclosure identifying the sponsor.
facts.quote: At minimum, all political ads need a "paid for by" disclosure identifying the sponsor.

facts.fact: Political ad disclosure requirements vary by state and platform.
facts.quote: Requirements vary by state and platform.

facts.fact: Most streaming platforms review political ads before they air and have their own compliance requirements.
facts.quote: Most streaming platforms also review political ads before they air and have their own compliance requirements.
